state_of_the_evidence.claim: Silero‑VAD gate reduces CPU usage on the development workstation
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: DEVICE‑GENERALISATION warm run: gated watcher uses 0.23 % of a core versus ungated watcher 39.1 % of a core (ADOPTION‑PLAN table, six non‑speech signals, 1 thread). Null hypothesis: no reduction (cost equal).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: The adaptive watcher labels non‑speech audio as speech at a very high rate
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: ADOPTION‑PLAN table: for six non‑speech fixtures (steady hum, fan, keyboard, music triad, white noise, near‑silence) the watcher reports 89 % “speech” (interval 89 % ± 0 %). Null hypothesis: 0 % speech on non‑speech signals.

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Composing row‑band removal with a 3‑frame temporal median cuts the occupied‑flip rate to 0.0014 % (≈21× improvement over row‑only)
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: combined_filter_results.json – variant “row+median3” on occupied capture: occupied flip = 0.0014 % (interval 0.0014 %). Row‑only flip = 0.0299 % (null).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Cloud multimodal model (Llama‑3.2‑Vision‑11B) achieves a usable margin of +0.667 over the silent class on corrected frames
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: cloud_multimodal_results.json – sensitivity 0.667 (8/12 speaking frames), false‑positive rate 0.0, margin = +0.667 (interval +0.667). Null hypothesis: margin ≤ 0 (no discrimination).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Row‑band removal on the corrected corpus raises the occupied‑flip rate to 1.790 % (i.e. it harms the signal)
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: row_band_removal_results.json – condition “occupied, row‑filter”: flip = 1.790 % (interval 1.790 %). Null hypothesis: filter would not increase flip (≤ 0.625 % observed without filter).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Dialogue‑intake hand‑off counting is inverted – it reports zero hand‑offs on a corpus that contains eight
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: dialogue_intake_selftest_results.json – synthetic real‑dialogue corpus with 8 canonical hand‑offs yields detected hand‑offs = 0 (interval 0). Null hypothesis: detected hand‑offs > 0.

state_of_the_evidence.claim: A 4‑th order high‑pass / notch does not improve pitch tracking in the presence of mains‑hum
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: notch_ab_results.json – emitted hz_p05 on speech + hum mixtures unchanged relative to unfiltered baseline; decision rule requires R ≥ 0.90 and SHIFT < 10 cents, both not met. Null hypothesis: notch reduces pitch error.

state_of_the_evidence.claim: GATE_FIELD does not under‑report the gate’s peak (the alleged 14.5× bug is withdrawn)
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: gate_peak_verdict_results.json – whole‑signal max = 0.7293, per‑record max = 0.0503; re‑analysis shows both intervals are comparable, ratio ≈ 1.0. Null hypothesis: gate under‑reports by >10×.

unsafe_claims.claim: Watcher CPU cost is 31.8 % of a core
unsafe_claims.why: No experiment ever produced this number; the only measured costs are 39.1 % (ungated) and 0.23 % (gated). The 31.8 % figure appears only in prose and contradicts all recorded measurements.
unsafe_claims.action: Remove the claim from all documentation and replace with the measured values.

unsafe_claims.claim: Silero‑VAD gate removes a 14.5× camera‑drift artifact (GATE_FIELD bug)
unsafe_claims.why: Retracted in GATE‑PEAK‑COVERAGE.md after showing the comparison used different intervals; the gate reports the correct peak.
unsafe_claims.action: Delete the claim and any downstream arguments that depend on it.

unsafe_claims.claim: ASCII‑motion character delta measures subject motion (48.19 % vs 50.00 % empty‑room)
unsafe_claims.why: EMPTY‑ROOM‑CONTROL.md shows the empty‑room flip rate is the theoretical maximum (50 %); the delta is camera exposure drift, not motion. The claim is falsified by the control.
unsafe_claims.action: Discard the motion‑interpretation of ASCII‑motion and stop using it as evidence of subject movement.

unsafe_claims.claim: Row‑band removal cleanly eliminates banding without side‑effects
unsafe_claims.why: ROW‑BAND‑REMOVAL.md (post‑correction) shows that on correctly read frames the filter raises occupied flip from 0.625 % to 1.790 %, i.e. it harms the signal.
unsafe_claims.action: Cease applying the row‑band filter; revert to raw representation.

unsafe_claims.why: The margin was measured on torn frames; after correcting the stride the margin is +0.667. The +0.455 figure is obsolete and misleading.
unsafe_claims.action: Update all reports to the corrected margin (+0.667) and note the previous value’s retraction.

unsafe_claims.claim: Silero‑VAD gate’s CPU advantage (≈31.8 %) is a real, machine‑independent benefit
unsafe_claims.why: The 31.8 % figure is unmeasured; DEVICE‑GENERALISATION shows the advantage varies with hardware and cache state. No single, reproducible number exists.
unsafe_claims.action: Replace the claim with the measured warm‑run ratio (0.23 % vs 39.1 %) and qualify it as hardware‑specific.

next_experiment.title: Cache‑Pressure Gate‑Cost Test
next_experiment.hypothesis: Under severe cache pressure on a low‑L2 device, the Silero‑VAD gate’s CPU‑usage advantage over the ungated watcher shrinks to less than a 1.5× reduction.
next_experiment.method: Run the watcher on a Raspberry Pi 4 (2 MiB L2, 1 GiB RAM) processing a 30 s audio clip (alice01_excerpt.wav) in three configurations: (1) ungated YIN only, (2) gated (Silero‑VAD + YIN), (3) gated plus an artificial memory‑pressure workload (large dummy array accesses) to force L2 eviction. Measure CPU time with `resource.getrusage` (utime+stime) per second of audio, repeat each configuration 5 times, report median and 95 % CI.
controls: Minimal L1‑resident loop (32 KiB) timed under identical cache‑pressure conditions – verifies the pressure apparatus works.
Ungated watcher on the same hardware – provides the baseline cost.
Gated watcher with no extra pressure – provides the ideal‑condition cost.
next_experiment.margin_threshold: The gated configuration must achieve a cost ratio ≤ 0.67 (i.e. ≥ 1.5× lower CPU usage) compared to ungated under the same pressure; the ratio is measured against the ungated baseline.
next_experiment.falsifier: If the observed cost ratio under pressure is ≥ 0.90 (i.e. < 1.1× advantage) or the gated configuration costs more than the ungated one, the hypothesis is falsified.

debrief.biggest_risk: Residual frame‑stride bugs still hidden in any script that reads NV12 captures; re‑running analyses on the corrected corpus may reveal further invalidated results, wasting a week of work.
debrief.what_would_change_the_plan: A successful demonstration that the Silero‑VAD gate retains a strong CPU‑usage advantage on target low‑resource hardware (or, conversely, a clear failure) would pivot the roadmap: a confirmed advantage would green‑light deployment of the gated watcher on edge devices; a failure would force a redesign of the front‑end (e.g., a different low‑cost VAD or hardware‑accelerated pitch tracker). Additionally, discovering a reliable motion signal (e.g., via a new camera sensor or a different visual feature) that survives all controls would unlock the teacher pipeline and shift focus to multimodal learning.
